L2=H^0(Ttor), with ||f||_2^2=(2*pi)^(-1) integral |f|^2 dx. More generally L^p uses the same normalized measure; L^infinity is essential supremum. argument.text: From D024 and D003, for every real s and periodic distribution h, the squared Hsrc^s norm is 2*pi times the squared H^s norm. Hence the identity on polynomials extends to inverse identity maps of the completions, agreeing as distributions; it preserves zero mean and reality. Consequently ||h||_(Hsrc^s)=sqrt(2*pi)||h||_(H^s), including s=0 and the L2src/L2 identity by D025 and D004. argument.text: First record two local facts. From D003 and D024, the squared source Sobolev norm is 2*pi times the squared target Sobolev norm at every real order. The identity on polynomials preserves Cauchy sequences and zero-distance equivalence when a norm is multiplied by the fixed positive scalar sqrt(2*pi); it therefore identifies their completions, with identical distributional Fourier coefficients. Consequently the carriers agree and ||h||_(Hsrc^s)=sqrt(2*pi)||h||_(H^s). At order zero, D004 and D025 give the same identity for L2src and L2. These identifications preserve zero mean. Also, whenever r<=s, each weight (1+k^2)^r is at most (1+k^2)^s; comparison of the nonnegative sums gives H^s contained in H^r with ||h||_(H^r)<=||h||_(H^s), and the analogous source inequality. These comparisons hold on the completions as well, by the identity extension. Next use only the epsilon quantifiers of E003 and E004 at sigma_s=1/2. Each phrase 'any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0' supplies a positive upper threshold below which every positive epsilon is admissible. The intersection of these two intervals and (0,1/8] contains a positive number: half the minimum of their two positive thresholds and 1/8 is one such number. Hence F002 follows without claiming that 1/8 itself is admissible. This existence assertion involves only the fixed source statements at sigma_s=1/2, not any datum, grid or support.

produces.statement: For every real s, Hsrc^s and H^s have the same periodic distributions and ||h||_(Hsrc^s)=sqrt(2*pi)||h||_(H^s); zero mean is preserved. At s=0 these are L2src and L2. For real r<=s, H^s is contained in H^r and ||h||_(H^r)<=||h||_(H^s), with the same assertion for source norms.

There exists a real eps with 0<eps<=1/8 admissible simultaneously for E003 and E004 at sigma_s=1/2: E003 holds with beta0=-1/2-eps for every beta in its displayed interval and all data and steps satisfying its other conditions, and E004 holds with a(1/2)=eps for all functions satisfying its other conditions. This choice can be made independently of all functions, grids, times and support.

argument.text: Choose once eps as in F002; keep this fixed through the stage argument. Fix arbitrary periodic f,g and assume L1: f belongs to H^gamma and g belongs to H^agamma. H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. Apply E004 with sigma_s=gamma, source g=f and source h=g. If gamma<1/2 its required second exponent is 1/2-gamma=agamma, and if gamma>1/2 it is 0=agamma. If gamma=1/2, use epsilon=eps, which is admissible by F002. The required second exponent is then eps, rather than agamma=1/8. Since eps<=1/8, F001 gives g in H^eps and ||g||_(H^eps)<=||g||_(H^(1/8)). In all cases F001 supplies the actual source memberships and converts the source inequality, leaving a factor sqrt(2*pi) in its constant. Thus ||fg||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^agamma). At gamma=1/2 the constant may depend on the single fixed eps chosen solely from the two source statements; it is independent of f,g and all numerical data. Discharge L1 and quantify f,g to obtain the unrestricted product assertion.

Fix arbitrary real M0,tau,t, nonnegative integer n and periodic w. Assume L2: 0<tau<=1, t in [n*tau,(n+1)*tau], and w is time-independent, mean-zero, belongs to H^gamma and satisfies ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. In particular M0>=0. H002 and F001 give 0<gamma<=1 and w in Hsrc^gamma with ||w||_(Hsrc^gamma)<=sqrt(2*pi)*M0. In E003 set sigma_s=gamma, tau_s=tau, j=n, t_j=n*tau and g1=g2=w. For gamma=1/2 use epsilon=eps from F002, so beta0=-1/2-eps; otherwise use the source's prescribed beta0. The source integral is Stage_n(t;w): D005 identifies exp(s partial_x^3)=S_(-s) and exp(-s partial_x^3)=S_s, D016 identifies the integrand, and D021 has the same integral and factor 1/2. This equality holds on polynomials and for the distributional stage by extension; the source bounds provide its bounded extension in the norms used here. Apply E003 first with beta=agamma. For gamma<1/2, beta0=2*gamma-3/2 and agamma=1/2-gamma, giving agamma-beta0=2-3*gamma>0, agamma<=1+gamma, and theta=(1/2+2*gamma)/(5/2-gamma). Its denominator is positive, and theta>=gamma since the numerator minus gamma times the denominator is (gamma-1/4)^2+7/16>0. For gamma=1/2, beta0=-1/2-eps<agamma=1/8<3/2, and theta=(11/8)/(2+eps). Since 0<eps<=1/8, theta>=11/17>1/2=gamma. For gamma>1/2, beta0=gamma-1<=0=agamma<=1+gamma and theta=(1+gamma)/2>=gamma because gamma<=1. Thus each beta is allowed and each exponent denominator is positive. After F001 converts both sides, E003 yields ||Stage_n(t;w)||_(H^agamma)<=C_gamma*tau^theta*||w||_(H^gamma)^2. Because 0<tau<=1 and theta>=gamma, tau^theta<=tau^gamma: (theta-gamma)log(tau)<=0. This gives the first pointwise bound by C_gamma*M0^2*tau^gamma. Apply E003 again to the same data with beta=1+gamma; this upper endpoint is allowed in all three cases and its time exponent is zero. Norm conversion gives ||Stage_n(t;w)||_(H^(1+gamma))<=C_gamma*M0^2. Both constants are uniform in n,tau,t and support by E003; any dependence on eps is on the single fixed choice in S002. Taking one larger constant depending only on M0,gamma gives both asserted bounds. The stage has continuous representatives in these norms: the E003 endpoint formula, boundedness of Dinv from H^gamma to H^(1+gamma), strong continuity of the Airy multipliers, and continuity of multiplication on H^(1+gamma) give this. For completeness, the inverse-derivative bound follows from (1+k^2)/k^2<=2 on nonzero modes. Strong continuity follows by finite Fourier truncation and uniformly small square-summable tails. For r=1+gamma>1/2, multiplication is bounded on H^r by the weighted convolution inequality <k>^r<=C_r(<l>^r+<k-l>^r), the ell^1-ell^2 convolution bound, and Cauchy-Schwarz with sum_k<k>^(-2*r)<infinity. These establish the endpoint formula's continuity and the polynomial extension; H^(1+gamma) embeds in H^agamma by F001. The pointwise estimates with a common constant therefore bound both time suprema on the step as specified by D004. Discharge L2 and universally quantify the arbitrary stage data. Together with S002 this proves exactly N007; the auxiliary eps does not occur in its assertion.

argument.text: D003 and D024 give ||h||_(Hsrc^s)^2=2*pi*||h||_(H^s)^2 at every real s. Multiplication of a norm by sqrt(2*pi)>0 preserves Cauchy sequences and zero-distance equivalence on polynomials. Thus the identity on polynomials identifies the completions as distributions with the same Fourier coefficients. It follows that ||h||_(Hsrc^s)=sqrt(2*pi)||h||_(H^s) and zero mean is preserved. D004 and D025 identify the order-zero spaces with L2 and L2src. For r<=s the weights satisfy (1+k^2)^r<=(1+k^2)^s, so comparison of the nonnegative sums yields H^s contained in H^r and ||h||_(H^r)<=||h||_(H^s); the source norms satisfy the identical comparison. This proves F001. To prove F002, interpret the sufficiently-small quantifiers in E003 and E004 at sigma_s=1/2: each guarantees a positive threshold such that every smaller positive epsilon is allowed in its estimate. Half the minimum of these thresholds and 1/8 is positive, is at most 1/8, and is below both thresholds. Therefore there exists a common admissible epsilon in (0,1/8]. Its existence and choice require only E003 and E004 with sigma_s=1/2, independently of functions, grids, times and support.

argument.text: Choose once eps as in F002; keep this fixed through the stage argument. Fix arbitrary periodic f,g and assume L1: f belongs to H^gamma and g belongs to H^agamma. H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. Apply E004 with sigma_s=gamma, source g=f and source h=g. If gamma<1/2 its required second exponent is 1/2-gamma=agamma, and if gamma>1/2 it is 0=agamma. If gamma=1/2, use epsilon=eps, which is admissible by F002. The required second exponent is then eps, rather than agamma=1/8. Since eps<=1/8, F001 gives g in H^eps and ||g||_(H^eps)<=||g||_(H^(1/8)). In all cases F001 supplies the actual source memberships and converts the source inequality, leaving a factor sqrt(2*pi) in its constant. Thus ||fg||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^agamma). At gamma=1/2 the constant may depend on the single fixed eps chosen solely from the two source statements; it is independent of f,g and all numerical data. Discharge L1 and quantify f,g to obtain the unrestricted product assertion.

Fix arbitrary real M0,tau,t, nonnegative integer n and periodic w. Assume L2: 0<tau<=1, t in [n*tau,(n+1)*tau], and w is time-independent, mean-zero, belongs to H^gamma and satisfies ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. In particular M0>=0. H002 and F001 give 0<gamma<=1 and w in Hsrc^gamma with ||w||_(Hsrc^gamma)<=sqrt(2*pi)*M0. In E003 set sigma_s=gamma, tau_s=tau, j=n, t_j=n*tau and g1=g2=w. For gamma=1/2 use epsilon=eps from F002, so beta0=-1/2-eps; otherwise use the source's prescribed beta0. The source integral is Stage_n(t;w): D005 identifies exp(s partial_x^3)=S_(-s) and exp(-s partial_x^3)=S_s, D016 identifies the integrand, and D021 has the same integral and factor 1/2. This equality holds on polynomials and for the distributional stage by extension; the source bounds provide its bounded extension in the norms used here. Apply E003 first with beta=agamma. For gamma<1/2, beta0=2*gamma-3/2 and agamma=1/2-gamma, giving agamma-beta0=2-3*gamma>0, agamma<=1+gamma, and theta=(1/2+2*gamma)/(5/2-gamma). Its denominator is positive, and theta>=gamma since the numerator minus gamma times the denominator is (gamma-1/4)^2+7/16>0. For gamma=1/2, beta0=-1/2-eps<agamma=1/8<3/2, and theta=(11/8)/(2+eps). Since 0<eps<=1/8, theta>=11/17>1/2=gamma. For gamma>1/2, beta0=gamma-1<=0=agamma<=1+gamma and theta=(1+gamma)/2>=gamma because gamma<=1. Thus each beta is allowed and each exponent denominator is positive. After F001 converts both sides, E003 yields ||Stage_n(t;w)||_(H^agamma)<=C_gamma*tau^theta*||w||_(H^gamma)^2. Because 0<tau<=1 and theta>=gamma, tau^theta<=tau^gamma: (theta-gamma)log(tau)<=0. This gives the first pointwise bound by C_gamma*M0^2*tau^gamma. Apply E003 again to the same data with beta=1+gamma; this upper endpoint is allowed in all three cases and its time exponent is zero. Norm conversion gives ||Stage_n(t;w)||_(H^(1+gamma))<=C_gamma*M0^2. Both constants are uniform in n,tau,t and support by E003; any dependence on eps is on the single fixed choice in S002. Taking one larger constant depending only on M0,gamma gives both asserted bounds. The stage has continuous representatives in these norms: the E003 endpoint formula, boundedness of Dinv from H^gamma to H^(1+gamma), strong continuity of the Airy multipliers, and continuity of multiplication on H^(1+gamma) give this. For completeness, the inverse-derivative bound follows from (1+k^2)/k^2<=2 on nonzero modes. Strong continuity follows by finite Fourier truncation and uniformly small square-summable tails. For r=1+gamma>1/2, multiplication is bounded on H^r by the weighted convolution inequality <k>^r<=C_r(<l>^r+<k-l>^r), the ell^1-ell^2 convolution bound, and Cauchy-Schwarz with sum_k<k>^(-2*r)<infinity. These establish the endpoint formula's continuity and the polynomial extension; H^(1+gamma) embeds in H^agamma by F001. The pointwise estimates with a common constant therefore bound both time suprema on the step as specified by D004. Discharge L2 and universally quantify the arbitrary stage data. Together with S002 this proves exactly N007; the auxiliary eps does not occur in its assertion.

argument.text: D003 and D024 give ||h||_(Hsrc^s)^2=2*pi*||h||_(H^s)^2 at every real s. Multiplication of a norm by sqrt(2*pi)>0 preserves Cauchy sequences and zero-distance equivalence on polynomials. Thus the identity on polynomials identifies the completions as distributions with the same Fourier coefficients. It follows that ||h||_(Hsrc^s)=sqrt(2*pi)||h||_(H^s) and zero mean is preserved. D004 and D025 identify the order-zero spaces with L2 and L2src. For r<=s the weights satisfy (1+k^2)^r<=(1+k^2)^s, so comparison of the nonnegative sums yields H^s contained in H^r and ||h||_(H^r)<=||h||_(H^s); the source norms satisfy the identical comparison.

argument.text: At sigma_s=1/2, the sufficiently-small clause of E003 means there exists d3>0 such that its estimate holds whenever 0<epsilon<d3, for all other parameters satisfying its hypotheses. Choose such a d3.
Similarly the sufficiently-small clause of E004 at sigma_s=1/2 gives d4>0 such that its product estimate holds whenever 0<epsilon<d4 for all functions in its specified spaces. Choose such a d4.
Since d3>0 and d4>0, min(d3,d4,1/8)/2>0. This number is at most 1/8 and is less than d3 and d4. Substitution in the universally quantified epsilon intervals established above yields F002.

produces.statement: There exists eps with 0<eps<=1/8 such that the following inequalities hold. For each beta in [-1/2-eps,3/2] there is C3 depending only on beta and eps such that, for every tau_s>0, nonnegative integer j, t in [j*tau_s,(j+1)*tau_s] and time-independent mean-zero g1,g2 in Hsrc^(1/2), ||(1/2) integral_(j*tau_s)^t S_(-s) partial_x[(S_s g1)(S_s g2)] ds||_(Hsrc^beta)<=C3*tau_s^((3/2-beta)/(2+eps))*||g1||_(Hsrc^(1/2))*||g2||_(Hsrc^(1/2)). There is also C4 depending only on eps such that, for every p in Hsrc^(1/2) and q in Hsrc^eps, ||p*q||_(L2src)<=C4*||p||_(Hsrc^(1/2))*||q||_(Hsrc^eps). The eps and constants are independent of the functions, grid indices, times, step sizes and support.

argument.text: Choose once eps as in F002; keep this fixed through the stage argument. Fix arbitrary periodic f,g and assume L1: f belongs to H^gamma and g belongs to H^agamma. H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. Apply E004 with sigma_s=gamma, source g=f and source h=g. If gamma<1/2 its required second exponent is 1/2-gamma=agamma, and if gamma>1/2 it is 0=agamma. If gamma=1/2, use epsilon=eps, which is admissible by F002. The required second exponent is then eps, rather than agamma=1/8. Since eps<=1/8, F001 gives g in H^eps and ||g||_(H^eps)<=||g||_(H^(1/8)). In all cases F001 supplies the actual source memberships and converts the source inequality, leaving a factor sqrt(2*pi) in its constant. Thus ||fg||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^agamma). At gamma=1/2 the constant may depend on the single fixed eps chosen solely from the two source statements; it is independent of f,g and all numerical data. Discharge L1 and quantify f,g to obtain the unrestricted product assertion.

Fix arbitrary real M0,tau,t, nonnegative integer n and periodic w. Assume L2: 0<tau<=1, t in [n*tau,(n+1)*tau], and w is time-independent, mean-zero, belongs to H^gamma and satisfies ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. In particular M0>=0. H002 and F001 give 0<gamma<=1 and w in Hsrc^gamma with ||w||_(Hsrc^gamma)<=sqrt(2*pi)*M0. In E003 set sigma_s=gamma, tau_s=tau, j=n, t_j=n*tau and g1=g2=w. For gamma=1/2 use epsilon=eps from F002, so beta0=-1/2-eps; otherwise use the source's prescribed beta0. The source integral is Stage_n(t;w): D005 identifies exp(s partial_x^3)=S_(-s) and exp(-s partial_x^3)=S_s, D016 identifies the integrand, and D021 has the same integral and factor 1/2. This equality holds on polynomials and for the distributional stage by extension; the source bounds provide its bounded extension in the norms used here. Apply E003 first with beta=agamma. For gamma<1/2, beta0=2*gamma-3/2 and agamma=1/2-gamma, giving agamma-beta0=2-3*gamma>0, agamma<=1+gamma, and theta=(1/2+2*gamma)/(5/2-gamma). Its denominator is positive, and theta>=gamma since the numerator minus gamma times the denominator is (gamma-1/4)^2+7/16>0. For gamma=1/2, beta0=-1/2-eps<agamma=1/8<3/2, and theta=(11/8)/(2+eps). Since 0<eps<=1/8, theta>=11/17>1/2=gamma. For gamma>1/2, beta0=gamma-1<=0=agamma<=1+gamma and theta=(1+gamma)/2>=gamma because gamma<=1. Thus each beta is allowed and each exponent denominator is positive. After F001 converts both sides, E003 yields ||Stage_n(t;w)||_(H^agamma)<=C_gamma*tau^theta*||w||_(H^gamma)^2. Because 0<tau<=1 and theta>=gamma, tau^theta<=tau^gamma: (theta-gamma)log(tau)<=0. This gives the first pointwise bound by C_gamma*M0^2*tau^gamma. Apply E003 again to the same data with beta=1+gamma; this upper endpoint is allowed in all three cases and its time exponent is zero. Norm conversion gives ||Stage_n(t;w)||_(H^(1+gamma))<=C_gamma*M0^2. Both constants are uniform in n,tau,t and support by E003; any dependence on eps is on the single fixed choice in S002. Taking one larger constant depending only on M0,gamma gives both asserted bounds. The stage has continuous representatives in these norms: the E003 endpoint formula, boundedness of Dinv from H^gamma to H^(1+gamma), strong continuity of the Airy multipliers, and continuity of multiplication on H^(1+gamma) give this. For completeness, the inverse-derivative bound follows from (1+k^2)/k^2<=2 on nonzero modes. Strong continuity follows by finite Fourier truncation and uniformly small square-summable tails. For r=1+gamma>1/2, multiplication is bounded on H^r by the weighted convolution inequality <k>^r<=C_r(<l>^r+<k-l>^r), the ell^1-ell^2 convolution bound, and Cauchy-Schwarz with sum_k<k>^(-2*r)<infinity. These establish the endpoint formula's continuity and the polynomial extension; H^(1+gamma) embeds in H^agamma by F001. The pointwise estimates with a common constant therefore bound both time suprema on the step as specified by D004. Discharge L2 and universally quantify the arbitrary stage data. Together with the product estimate, these are all the required assertions; the auxiliary eps does not occur in them.
